recommendations.rationale: The retained evidence cannot separate a solver/objective explanation (early User_Requested_Stop solves and holding_tip_speed_weight=0.0 / terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.0) from an execution/model explanation for the 0.63-1.58 m/s late tip speed, so no control-parameter change is asserted now. The single bounded saved-state check (model.gvs@1.0.0, horizon_s 0.01, implicit_euler, integration_step_s 0.002, max_checks 1, max_wall_s 300, local_solves 6 / prediction_evaluations 24) using operation prediction_braking would discriminate: roll out the saved update-34 state under the recorded applied tensions and, via local_comparison, under a zero-input coast over 0.01 s, and compare the predicted tip-speed change to the recorded 1.58 m/s late speed. If recorded tensions predict a substantial speed reduction that did not occur, the model-execution explanation strengthens; if they also predict high speed, the objective/authority explanation strengthens. Any later adoption of a specific parameter/value (e.g. holding_tip_speed_weight within [0.0001, 1.0]) would require a separate matched design adoption and is not authorized here.

attribution.reason: The recorded sampled-settling failure coincides with late-window tip speeds of 0.63-1.58 m/s at the same samples where the 0.02 m/s criterion applies and the 0.01 m error bound is met only at the final sample; this is an observed association in the retained evidence.

Recorded per-update optimization_solve_s of 2.89-6.75 s exceed the 0.01 s control period and account for the wall-clock mean_update_s of 17.08 s with 35/35 deadline misses; the scheduling note states wall-clock deadline misses do not inject physical delay into simulated time, so this is a real-time-feasibility observation distinct from settling.

34 of 35 updates are classified User_Requested_Stop with policy_stop_reason relative_seed_improvement (e.g. update 30 at iteration 16), which is consistent with the solver returning early rather than driving the tip speed down, but retained evidence contains no warm plans or optimizer iterations, so its contribution to the late speed is not established.

The bound controller recipe records holding_tip_speed_weight=0.0 and terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.0, i.e. no explicit tip-speed penalty, which is consistent with the observed high late speed; however no optimizer iterations or objective traces are retained, so a contribution to the settling failure cannot be demonstrated from this evidence alone.

The two available aligned one-step comparisons are marked 'aligned' with tip differences of 0.0062 m and 0.0012 m, which weakens a large model-execution mismatch as the dominant explanation for the late speed, though only two intervals are recorded.

facts.statement: The saved summary reports reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m=0.007642608585867386 m inside reach_tolerance_m=0.01 m, while sampled_settling_passed=false: late_max_error_m=0.05813810428573256 m and late_max_speed_m_s=1.5810152739742807 m/s exceed the recorded settling criteria position_limit_m=0.01 m, speed_limit_m_s=0.02 m/s over window_s=0.05 s; terminal_speed_m_s at the end of the window is 0.6351726092425104 m/s. Reach, sampled settling and real-time feasibility are recorded as separate outcomes.

The late-motion trace over [0.30, 0.35] s records world-tip speed of 0.861872864376846 m/s at t=0.30, peaks at 1.5810152739742807 m/s at t=0.33, and is still 0.6351726092425104 m/s at t=0.35; tip error falls monotonically from 0.05813810428573256 m (t=0.30) to 0.007642608585867386 m (t=0.35). So the 0.02 m/s speed limit is exceeded at every recorded late sample while the 0.01 m position limit is reached only at the final sample.

The saved summary records control_period_s=0.01, deadline_misses=35 (all updates), mean_update_s=17.075238151415917 s, and stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop=34 with Solve_Succeeded=1.
